recipes.name: Karachi chicken biryani
recipes.intro: Layered, fragrant and fiery, with the potato and dried plum that make it unmistakably Karachi.
ing: 4 green chillies, a handful each of mint and coriander
Pinch of saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk
1/2 cup oil or ghee, plus whole spices: bay leaf, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon
steps: Fry the onions in the oil until deep golden. Lift out half for layering.
Add ginger-garlic paste and chicken; sear for 5 minutes. Stir in tomatoes, yogurt, masala, potatoes and plums. Cover and cook 25 minutes until the oil rises to the top.
Boil the rice in heavily salted water with the whole spices until three-quarters done, then drain.
Layer half the rice, all the chicken, the mint, coriander, chillies and fried onions, then the rest of the rice. Drizzle with saffron milk.
Seal the lid and cook on the lowest heat (dum) for 20 minutes. Rest 5 minutes, then fold gently from the sides.
recipes.tip: Salt the rice water until it tastes like the sea. The rice only takes in a little.

recipes.name: Beef biryani
recipes.intro: Deep, meaty and celebratory. The biryani that turns up at every big family wedding.
ing: Saffron milk, mint, coriander, green chillies
steps: Marinate the beef in yogurt, ginger-garlic and masala for 2 hours.
Cook it with half the fried onions and the tomatoes, covered, until tender, about 75 minutes.
Parboil the rice in salted water with whole spices.
Layer rice and beef with herbs, fried onions, saffron and kewra.
Seal and steam on low for 25 minutes.
recipes.tip: Beef needs to be fully tender before layering. It won't soften further on dum.

recipes.name: Kabuli pulao
recipes.intro: Peshawar's gentle, golden pulao: meat cooked into its own stock, crowned with glossy carrots and raisins.
ing: 1 kg lamb or beef on the bone
steps: Brown the onions deeply in oil. Add the meat and sear well.
Add 8 cups water, cumin, garam masala and salt. Simmer covered for about an hour until tender.
In another pan, sauté carrots with the sugar until glossy, add raisins and almonds until the raisins puff.
Measure 4½ cups of the stock back in with the meat, bring to a boil, add the drained rice and cook until the water drops below the rice.
Scatter the carrots and raisins on top, cover tightly and steam on low for 20 minutes.
recipes.tip: Fry the onions darker than feels right. That colour is where the pulao's golden hue comes from.

recipes.name: Yakhni chicken pulao
recipes.intro: Rice cooked in a fragrant chicken stock with whole spices. Subtle, comforting and never fussy.
ing: Potli: 1 tbsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp fennel, 4 cloves garlic, 1 inch ginger
Whole spices: cumin, cloves, cardamom, peppercorns, bay leaf
steps: Simmer the chicken with the potli spices in 6 cups water for 35 minutes to make the yakhni.
Fry the onion golden in ghee with the whole spices; add the chicken pieces and yogurt.
Pour in 4½ cups strained yakhni and bring to a boil.
Add the rice, cook until the water dips below, then steam covered on low for 15 minutes.
recipes.tip: Tie the potli spices in muslin so the stock stays clear and the rice stays white.

recipes.name: Matar pulao
recipes.intro: The weeknight pulao: sweet peas, whole spices and rice that stays in perfect separate grains.
ing: Whole spices: 4 cloves, 2 cardamom, 1 bay leaf, small cinnamon stick
steps: Fry the onion in ghee until golden with the cumin and whole spices.
Add the peas, chilli and salt and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring to a rolling boil and add the drained rice.
Cook on high until the water sinks below the surface of the rice, then cover and steam on low for 15 minutes.
recipes.tip: Leave the lid shut for the full 15 minutes. Every peek lets the steam out.

recipes.name: Lahori chicken karahi
recipes.intro: No onions, no water, just tomatoes, a ferocious flame and the smell of a Lahore food street at midnight.
ing: Ginger matchsticks and fresh coriander to finish
steps: Heat the oil in a karahi until shimmering. Sear the chicken on high until it turns white, then add the ginger-garlic paste.
Lay the tomatoes on top skin side up, cover for 5 minutes, then pull off the skins and mash the tomatoes into the pan.
Add the crushed spices and salt and keep stirring on high (bhunai) for about 15 minutes, until the oil separates.
Finish with green chillies, black pepper, ginger and coriander.
recipes.tip: Keep the flame high the whole way. Karahi wants fierce heat and no water.

recipes.name: Shinwari chicken karahi
recipes.intro: The Peshawar highway classic from the Shinwari tribe: chicken seared in fat with salt and tomatoes, finished with black pepper, green chillies and ginger. No powdered spices, no onions, all flavour.
ing: 1/2 cup ghee or animal fat (charbi), or oil
Fresh coriander and lemon to serve
steps: Heat the ghee in a heavy karahi on high until very hot. Add the chicken and salt and sear for 6 to 8 minutes until golden on all sides.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste for a minute, then lay the tomatoes on top, skin side up. Cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Pull off the tomato skins with tongs and mash the tomatoes into the pan.
Cook uncovered on high, stirring and scraping, for 10 to 12 minutes until the tomatoes melt into a glossy sauce and the fat separates.
Add the black pepper and green chillies, cook 2 minutes more, then finish with ginger and coriander. Serve straight from the karahi with naan and lemon.
recipes.tip: The magic is in the fat and the flame. Keep the heat high and don't add water or powdered spices.

recipes.name: Shahi chicken qorma
recipes.intro: The royal centrepiece of every Pakistani wedding and Eid dawat: chicken slow-cooked in yogurt, brown onions and whole spices, enriched with almond paste and finished with kewra.
ing: Whole spices: 2 bay leaves, 6 cloves, 4 green cardamom, 1 black cardamom, 1 cinnamon stick
10 to 12 almonds, soaked and ground to a paste
A few drops of kewra water
Slivered almonds, ginger matchsticks and coriander to garnish
steps: Fry the onions in the oil until deep golden brown. Lift them out, cool, then crush or blend with a splash of yogurt into a smooth brown-onion paste.
In the same oil, crackle the whole spices for 30 seconds. Add the chicken and ginger-garlic paste and sear for 5 minutes.
Mix the yogurt with the chilli, coriander, turmeric and salt. Add to the pan and cook on medium, stirring, until the oil starts to separate.
Stir in the brown-onion paste and almond paste with 1 cup of water. Cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Sprinkle over the garam masala and kewra, cover for 5 minutes on the lowest heat (dum), then garnish with almonds, ginger and coriander. Serve with naan or sheermal.
recipes.tip: The brown onions make the qorma. Fry them slowly to an even deep gold; if they burn, the gravy turns bitter.

recipes.name: Chicken handi
recipes.intro: Creamy, mellow and fragrant with dried fenugreek, cooked and served in its clay pot.
ing: 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric
steps: Fry the onions until light golden, then add the ginger-garlic paste and chicken.
Add tomatoes, chilli, turmeric and salt and cook down for 10 minutes.
Stir in the yogurt and cook until the oil separates.
Lower the heat, add the cream, garam masala and crushed kasuri methi, and simmer 5 minutes.
recipes.tip: Rub the kasuri methi between your palms as it goes in. It wakes up the oils.

recipes.name: Chicken tikka
recipes.intro: Charred at the edges, tender inside, and smoked with a single piece of coal.
ing: 1 kg chicken leg pieces, deeply scored
1 tsp each cumin and coriander powder
steps: Mix everything except the charcoal and marinate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Roast at 230°C for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, or grill over coals.
Heat the charcoal until glowing, set it in a small steel bowl inside the pan, drizzle with oil and cover for 3 minutes.
Serve with lemon, onion rings and green chutney.
recipes.tip: Score right to the bone so the marinade reaches all the way through.

recipes.name: Full chicken broast
recipes.intro: Pakistan's favourite fried chicken: a whole bird marinated in lemon and spice, steamed until tender, then fried to a deep, crackling crust. Served with fries, garlic mayo and ketchup.
ing: 1 whole chicken (1.2 to 1.4 kg), skin on, cut into quarters
Marinade: 3 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp white pepper, 1 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp vinegar
Coating: 1½ cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup cornflour, 1 tsp each salt, red chilli and white pepper, 1/2 tsp baking powder
1 egg beaten with 1/2 cup cold milk
To serve: fries, garlic mayo, ketchup, onion rings and lemon
steps: Score the chicken deeply, rub in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Steam the pieces over boiling water for 20 minutes until just cooked through, then let them cool and dry for 10 minutes.
Mix the coating ingredients. Dip each piece in the egg and milk, then press firmly into the flour. Repeat once more for an extra-crunchy crust.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry two pieces at a time for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on a rack, sprinkle with chilli and salt, and serve hot with fries and dips.
recipes.tip: Restaurants pressure-fry broast in special fryers. Never fry in a home pressure cooker; steaming first gives you the same juicy meat safely.

recipes.name: Royal beef nihari
recipes.intro: Beef shank simmered overnight into a glossy, spiced stew. Finished at the table with ginger, chilli and lemon.
ing: To serve: ginger matchsticks, green chillies, lemon, coriander, fried onions
steps: Fry the onions in ghee until golden; lift out half for garnish.
Add the beef and ginger-garlic paste and sear on all sides. Stir in the masala for 2 minutes.
Add the water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 5 to 6 hours (or 90 minutes in a pressure cooker).
Whisk the atta into a cup of water, pour it in slowly while stirring, and simmer 20 minutes until silky.
For the tarka, heat 2 tbsp ghee with a pinch of masala and chilli, pour over and garnish.
recipes.tip: Start it the night before. Nihari was always a dawn breakfast.

recipes.name: Karachi beef haleem
recipes.intro: Wheat, five lentils and beef slow-cooked and beaten together until it pulls into long, silky strands, then crowned with crisp fried onions, ginger, green chillies and lemon. Karachi's Ramadan favourite.
ing: 1/4 cup each masoor, moong and urad daal
2 tsp red chilli, 1 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp garam masala
To serve: fried onions, ginger, green chilli, lemon, chaat masala
steps: Boil the wheat, barley and lentils with turmeric in plenty of water until very soft, about 90 minutes.
Separately cook the beef with onions, ginger-garlic, spices and water for about 2 hours, until it falls apart.
Combine both pots and beat with a wooden ghotna or a whisk on low heat for 30 to 45 minutes until stringy.
Serve with all the garnishes on the side.
recipes.tip: A potato masher, then a whisk, gets you close to the ghotna's strands.

recipes.name: Peshawari beef karahi
recipes.intro: Namak Mandi style: beef, tomatoes, salt and fat, cooked hard and fast. Simple and magnificent.
ing: 1 kg beef with some fat, small cubes
steps: Sear the beef in very hot fat with salt until browned.
Add 1 cup water, cover and cook until tender, about 40 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, peel off the skins as they soften, and mash.
Cook on high until the fat separates; finish with pepper, ginger and chillies.
recipes.tip: Peshawari karahi uses almost no spice. The flavour comes from good beef and patience.

recipes.name: Shinwari dumba karahi
recipes.intro: The pride of Peshawar's Namak Mandi: bone-in dumba (fat-tailed lamb) seared in its own fat with salt and tomatoes, then finished with black pepper, green chillies and ginger. Simple, rich and unforgettable.
ing: 1 kg dumba (lamb) on the bone, small pieces
Fresh coriander, lemon and naan to serve
steps: Melt the dumba fat in a heavy karahi on high heat until it renders and sizzles.
Add the lamb and salt and sear hard for 8 to 10 minutes until browned on all sides.
Stir in the ginger-garlic paste, add 1 cup of water, cover and cook on medium for 35 to 40 minutes until the meat is tender.
Lay the tomatoes on top, cover for 5 minutes, then peel off the skins and mash them into the pan.
Cook uncovered on high, stirring, until the tomatoes melt into the fat and the oil separates, about 10 minutes.
Finish with black pepper, green chillies, ginger and coriander. Serve hot from the karahi.
recipes.tip: Shinwari karahi uses no powdered spices. Good lamb, its own fat, salt and a fierce flame are all it needs.

recipes.name: Roghni naan
recipes.intro: Soft, milky naan glazed with egg and showered with sesame and nigella seeds.
ing: Sesame and nigella seeds, butter to finish
steps: Knead the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk, yogurt and oil into a soft dough, adding water as needed, for 8 minutes.
Cover and leave to rise for an hour.
Divide into 6, press each into an oval and dimple with your fingertips.
Brush with egg wash and scatter the seeds.
Bake on a very hot stone at 250°C for 6 to 8 minutes, then brush with butter.
recipes.tip: No oven stone? Cook on a hot tawa, then hold it over the open flame to blister.

recipes.name: Balochi-style tandoori kaak
recipes.intro: Inspired by the rustic breads of Balochistan, this golden, seeded flatbread has a beautifully browned crust and a tender centre. Fresh from the oven, it pairs wonderfully with curries, chutneys and a warm cup of chai.
ing: 2 tbsp vegetable oil or melted ghee
3/4 to 1 cup lukewarm water, as needed
Melted butter or ghee for brushing
steps: Prepare the dough: mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Add the yogurt, oil and enough lukewarm water to make a soft dough. Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth.
Let it rise: cover and rest in a warm place for 45 to 60 minutes, until noticeably expanded.
Shape the bread: divide into 2 or 3 portions. Flatten into thick rounds, press the centres slightly and score a decorative pattern. Sprinkle with sesame and kalonji.
Bake until golden: preheat the oven to 230°C. Bake on a preheated tray or pizza stone for 12 to 18 minutes, depending on thickness, until cooked through and golden brown.
Finish and serve: brush lightly with melted ghee and serve warm with chai, yogurt, chutney or your favourite curry.
recipes.tip: Traditional Balochi kaak is cooked around heated stones or over an open fire, and the method varies by community. This oven-baked version recreates the seeded bread pictured here, not the stone-cooked original.

recipes.name: Lachha paratha
recipes.intro: Flaky, layered and crisp, coiled from a pleated sheet of dough and ghee.
steps: Knead a soft dough and rest it for 20 minutes.
Roll a thin circle, spread with ghee and dust with flour.
Pleat it like a paper fan, then coil the strip into a spiral and rest 10 minutes.
Roll gently and cook on a hot tawa with ghee until crisp on both sides.
Crush lightly between your palms to open the layers.
recipes.tip: Resting the coil is what keeps the layers from sealing together.

recipes.name: Pakistani tawa roti
recipes.intro: Soft, puffed whole-wheat roti. The bread of every Pakistani dinner table.
steps: Knead the atta and water into a soft dough and rest for 20 minutes.
Roll thin circles with a light dusting of flour.
Cook on a hot tawa until bubbles appear, flip, then press the edges so it puffs.
Brush with ghee and keep wrapped in a cloth.
recipes.tip: Softer dough makes softer roti. It should feel like an earlobe.

recipes.name: Daal chana
recipes.intro: Split chickpeas cooked soft but whole, finished with a sizzling garlic tarka.
ing: Tarka: 3 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 3 dried red chillies, 4 garlic cloves sliced
steps: Boil the daal with turmeric until soft but holding its shape, about 40 minutes.
Fry the onion, add ginger-garlic, tomatoes, chilli and salt and cook down.
Combine and simmer 10 minutes.
Heat the ghee, crackle the cumin, chillies and garlic, and pour over the daal.
recipes.tip: Pour the tarka on at the table so everyone hears it.

recipes.name: Daal masoor
recipes.intro: The red lentil daal of every Pakistani home, ready in half an hour.
ing: Tarka: 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 3 garlic cloves, 2 dried red chillies
steps: Boil the lentils with water, tomato, turmeric, chilli and salt for 20 minutes.
Whisk until smooth, adding a splash of water if needed.
Make the tarka and pour it over. Finish with coriander.
recipes.tip: Serve with plain rice, a little achar and a sliced onion.

recipes.name: Moong daal
recipes.intro: Yellow, gentle and quick. The daal mothers make when someone needs looking after.
ing: Tarka: 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, pinch of hing, 2 garlic cloves
steps: Simmer the daal with turmeric, tomato, chilli and salt for 25 minutes until soft.
Whisk lightly so it is creamy but still has texture.
Pour over the tarka and finish with coriander.
recipes.tip: A squeeze of lemon at the end brightens the whole pot.

recipes.name: Chana chaat
recipes.intro: Chickpeas tossed with onion, tomato, cucumber, tangy imli and green chutney, finished with crunchy papdi and sev. The taste of every iftar table.
ing: 1 tsp chaat masala, 1/2 tsp roasted cumin, 1/2 tsp red chilli
Juice of 1/2 lemon, salt to taste
A handful of papdi (crisp wafers) and sev
steps: Toss the chickpeas and potato with chaat masala, cumin, chilli, salt and lemon juice.
Fold in the onion, tomato and cucumber.
Spoon over the imli and green chutneys without stirring them in completely.
Top with crushed papdi, sev and coriander, and serve straight away.
recipes.tip: Add the papdi and sev at the very last moment so they stay crunchy.

recipes.name: Golgappay
recipes.intro: Crisp, hollow puris filled with spiced chickpeas and potato, then flooded with tangy imli water. Pop the whole thing in one bite.
ing: Imli water: 1/2 cup tamarind pulp, 4 cups chilled water, 1 tsp roasted cumin, 1 tsp chaat masala, 1 tsp black salt, a handful of mint, 2 green chillies, sugar to taste
Imli chutney and green chutney to serve
Sev and fresh coriander to garnish
steps: Blend the mint and chillies with a little water, then mix with the tamarind pulp, chilled water, cumin, chaat masala, black salt and sugar. Chill for at least an hour.
Mix the chickpeas, potato and onion with a pinch of chaat masala and salt.
Just before serving, tap a small hole in the top of each puri with your thumb.
Fill each puri with a spoonful of the chickpea mix and a little imli chutney.
Dip into the imli water, top with sev and eat at once.
recipes.tip: Keep the imli water ice-cold and fill the puris only when you're ready to eat, or they go soft.

recipes.name: Mix vegetable pakora
recipes.intro: Lacy, crunchy fritters of onion, potato, spinach and green chilli bound in spiced besan. The taste of Ramadan iftar and rainy afternoons, best eaten hot with green chutney, imli and a cup of chai.
ing: 1 medium potato, cut into thin matchsticks
3 to 4 tbsp water, only if needed
Chaat masala, green chutney and imli chutney to serve
steps: Put the onions, potato, spinach, green chillies and coriander in a bowl with the salt. Squeeze everything together with your hands and leave for 10 minutes so the vegetables release their moisture.

Add the besan, rice flour, crushed chilli, crushed coriander, ajwain, cumin and turmeric. Mix into a thick, sticky dough that just coats the vegetables. Add a spoonful of water only if it's too dry; it should not be a runny batter.
Heat the oil over medium heat. Test it with a small piece of dough: it should sizzle and rise to the top without browning straight away.
Drop small, loose clusters of the mixture into the oil with your fingers, leaving them rough so the edges turn lacy. Don't crowd the pan.
Leave them for a minute to set, then turn and fry for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and crisp all over.
Drain on a rack, sprinkle with chaat masala and serve hot with green chutney, imli and chai.
recipes.tip: Let the vegetables' own water bind the dough. The less water you add, the crispier and less oily the pakoras will be.

recipes.name: Crispy aloo pakora
recipes.intro: Thin potato slices dipped in a spiced besan batter and fried until golden and crackling. The iftar favourite and the perfect rainy-day snack, served hot with green chutney and imli.
ing: 2 tbsp rice flour, for extra crunch
1/2 tsp chaat masala, plus extra to sprinkle
Green chutney and imli chutney to serve
steps: Soak the potato slices in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
Whisk the besan, rice flour, spices, coriander, green chilli and salt with enough cold water to make a smooth batter that coats the back of a spoon.
Heat the oil to 175°C. Dip each slice in the batter, let the excess drip off, and slide it into the oil.
Fry in small batches for 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on a rack, sprinkle with chaat masala and serve hot with green chutney and imli.
recipes.tip: Keep the slices thin and dry, and don't crowd the pan. Too many at once drops the oil temperature and the pakoras turn soggy.

recipes.name: Lal lobia masala
recipes.intro: Red kidney beans simmered in a deep, spiced onion and tomato masala until creamy and rich. Hearty, comforting and perfect with plain rice or roti.
ing: 1½ cups dried red kidney beans (lal lobia), soaked overnight, or 2 cans, drained
Green chillies, ginger matchsticks and coriander to garnish
steps: Drain the soaked beans, cover with fresh water and boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer for 45 to 60 minutes (or 15 to 20 minutes in a pressure cooker) until soft. Keep the cooking water.
Heat the oil, crackle the cumin seeds, then fry the onions until golden brown.
Add the ginger-garlic paste, then the tomatoes, chilli, coriander, turmeric and salt. Cook (bhunai) until the tomatoes break down and the oil separates.
Add the beans with 1½ cups of their cooking water. Simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few beans against the pot to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the garam masala and garnish with green chillies, ginger and coriander. Serve with rice or roti.
recipes.tip: Dried kidney beans must be boiled hard for at least 10 minutes before simmering. Never cook them in a slow cooker from raw.

recipes.name: Gulab jamun
recipes.intro: Milk dumplings fried slow and deep brown, soaked in cardamom and rose syrup.
ing: Syrup: 1½ cups sugar, 1½ cups water, 4 cardamom pods, 1 tsp rosewater
steps: Simmer the sugar and water for 8 minutes, add cardamom and rosewater, and keep warm.
Mix the dry ingredients with ghee and egg into a soft dough without kneading hard.
Roll into smooth balls with no cracks.
Fry on low heat, turning, until deep brown, about 8 minutes.
Drop into the warm syrup and soak for an hour.
recipes.tip: If the oil is too hot they brown outside and stay raw inside. Low and slow.

recipes.name: Rasmalai
recipes.intro: Soft cheese patties soaked in chilled saffron and cardamom milk. Light, elegant and festive.
steps: Boil 2 litres milk, curdle with lemon juice, drain and rinse the chenna; hang for 30 minutes.
Knead until smooth, shape 12 small discs.
Cook the discs in light sugar syrup for 12 minutes, covered.
Reduce 1 litre milk by a third with sugar, saffron and cardamom.
Squeeze the discs gently, soak in the milk and chill overnight.
recipes.tip: Knead the chenna until your palm feels greasy. That is when it's ready.

recipes.name: Shahi zarda
recipes.intro: The jewel of every Pakistani wedding and Eid table: fragrant basmati in red, yellow, green and white, steamed with ghee, saffron and cardamom, then crowned with cherries, raisins, almonds, pistachios and silver leaf.
ing: A pinch of saffron soaked in 2 tbsp warm milk
Food colours: yellow (or orange), red and green, a few drops each
steps: Boil the rice in plenty of water until three-quarters cooked, then drain well.
Split the rice into four portions. Mix yellow, red and green colour into three of them and leave one white.
Heat the ghee in a heavy pot, crackle the cardamom and cloves, then add the sugar with 1/4 cup water and stir until it melts into a light syrup.
Gently layer in all four colours of rice, then add the khoya, raisins, nuts and half the cherries. Fold once, very lightly, so the colours stay separate.
Drizzle over the saffron milk and kewra, cover tightly and steam on the lowest heat (dum) for 15 to 20 minutes until the syrup is absorbed.
Pile onto a platter and decorate with the rest of the cherries, nuts and silver leaf.
recipes.tip: Fold the coloured rice with a light hand, or it turns into one muddy colour. Long, separate grains are the mark of good zarda.

recipes.name: Fruit trifle custard
recipes.region: Creamy vanilla custard with fresh fruit
recipes.intro: The dessert of every Pakistani dawat and Eid table: chilled, silky vanilla custard folded with fresh banana, mango, strawberries, kiwi and grapes, then showered with pomegranate, almonds and pistachios.
ing: 1/2 cup red or green grapes, halved
2 tbsp each almonds and pistachios, slivered
steps: Mix the custard powder with 1/2 cup of the cold milk until completely smooth.
Bring the rest of the milk to a boil with the sugar, then lower the heat.
Pour in the custard mixture in a thin stream, stirring all the time, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until thick and glossy. Stir in the cardamom.
Press cling film onto the surface so no skin forms, cool to room temperature, then chill for at least 2 hours.
Just before serving, whisk the custard smooth and fold in the bananas, mango, strawberries, kiwi and grapes.
Top with pomegranate seeds, almonds and pistachios and serve cold.
recipes.tip: Add the fruit only when you're ready to serve. Bananas brown and fruit juices thin the custard if they sit too long.

recipes.name: Rice kheer
recipes.intro: Slow-cooked rice pudding with cardamom, almonds and a breath of kewra.
ing: 2 tbsp each almonds and pistachios, sliced
A few drops of kewra water
steps: Lightly crush the soaked rice.
Bring the milk to a boil, add the rice and simmer on low, stirring often, for 45 minutes until thick.
Add the sugar and cardamom and cook 10 minutes more.
Stir in the nuts and kewra and chill before serving.
recipes.tip: Serve in clay bowls (kunnay). They soak up a little moisture and set the top.

recipes.name: Gajar ka halwa
recipes.intro: Winter's red carrots cooked down in milk and ghee until jammy and rich.
steps: Cook the carrots in the milk, stirring, until all the milk evaporates, about 50 minutes.
Add the ghee and fry for 10 minutes.
Add the sugar and cook until it melts and is absorbed.
Stir in the khoya and cardamom, and top with nuts.
recipes.tip: Look for the deep red winter carrots. Orange ones taste fine but the colour is not the same.

recipes.name: Sheer khurma
recipes.intro: Vermicelli, milk and dates. The first thing served on Eid ul Fitr morning.
steps: Fry the vermicelli in ghee until golden.
Boil the milk with cardamom for 10 minutes.
Add the vermicelli, sugar and dates and simmer for 10 minutes.
Fry the nuts and raisins in a little ghee and stir them in. Serve warm or chilled.
recipes.tip: It thickens as it cools. Loosen with warm milk before serving guests.

recipes.name: Zeera raita
recipes.intro: Cool yogurt with roasted cumin, the partner to every biryani.
ing: Salt, mint and a pinch of chilli
steps: Whisk the yogurt smooth with a splash of water.
Fold in the onion, tomato and cucumber.
Season with salt and cumin and garnish with mint and chilli.
recipes.tip: Dry-roast the cumin seeds yourself. The smell is half the raita.

recipes.name: Mint, coriander and tomato chutney
recipes.region: Podina, sabz dhaniya aur tamatar ki chutney
recipes.intro: A fresh, spicy and tangy Pakistani green chutney made with mint, fresh coriander, tomatoes, green chillies and salt. Perfect with daal chawal, biryani, pakoras, samosas, kebabs and homemade roti.
ing: 1 cup fresh coriander (sabz dhaniya), with tender stems
steps: Wash the mint and coriander well and shake dry. Pick the mint leaves off their stems.
Add the herbs, green chillies, garlic, cumin, salt and lemon juice to a blender with a splash of cold water.
Blend in short bursts until coarse, then add half the tomato and pulse a few times.
Finely chop the rest of the tomato and stir it through for texture. Taste and adjust the salt, chilli and lemon.
recipes.tip: Use ice-cold water and short pulses so the blades don't heat the herbs. The chutney stays bright green for longer.

recipes.name: Mix aam ka achar
recipes.region: Raw mango, carrot and green chilli pickle
recipes.intro: The summer pickle of every Pakistani home: sour raw mango, sweet carrot and fiery green chillies in mustard oil with fennel, fenugreek and kalonji. A spoonful turns plain daal chawal into a feast.
ing: 1 kg raw green mangoes (keri), washed and dried
2 tbsp red chilli powder (or crushed red chilli)
1 tbsp fenugreek seeds (methi dana), lightly crushed
2 tbsp yellow mustard seeds, coarsely crushed
steps: Cut the mangoes into chunks with the skin on, discarding the soft seed. Toss with the carrots, chillies, 2 tbsp salt and the turmeric.
Spread on a clean cloth and dry in the sun, or in a very low oven, for 4 to 6 hours until the surfaces feel dry.
Heat the mustard oil until it just smokes, then let it cool until warm.
Mix all the spices and the remaining salt into the warm oil, then fold in the vegetables and vinegar so everything is coated.
Pack tightly into a clean, completely dry glass jar and pour over the remaining oil so the pickle is covered.
Keep the jar in a sunny spot and shake it once a day. It's ready in about a week and keeps for months.
recipes.tip: Every spoon, jar and cloth must be completely dry. A single drop of water will spoil the achar, and the oil should always sit above the pickle.

recipes.name: Mixed vegetable achar
recipes.intro: Tangy, oily and fiery. A spoonful turns plain daal chawal into a feast.
ing: 500 g mixed carrots, cauliflower and green chillies
1 tbsp fennel, 1 tsp fenugreek, 1 tsp nigella
2 tbsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp turmeric
steps: Cut the vegetables, salt them and dry in the sun or a low oven for a few hours.
Heat the mustard oil until it smokes, then cool slightly.
Mix the spices into the warm oil, then the vegetables and vinegar.
Pack into a clean jar and leave 3 days before eating.
recipes.tip: Every spoon going into the jar must be completely dry, or the achar will spoil.
